changes_made.explanation: Removed GPT-4o, GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4-turbo from models list as these are judges, not generation models being evaluated. Kept GPT-4 and Newbing as these are the reader/generator models. Removed duplicate MixInstruct (kept MIXINSTRUCT). Added clearer description of augmented outputs.

Normalized 'accuracy' to 'Accuracy'. Removed C2I and I2C as these are components/directions of Verdict Switch Rate, not separate metrics. Kept Accuracy and Verdict Switch Rate as the main automated evaluation metrics.

Removed 'reference-guided single evaluation' as redundant with 'single evaluation'. Kept all models as they are explicitly used as LLM judges. Criteria remains 'correctness' as this is the main evaluation criterion.

overall_notes: The paper clearly addresses NLG evaluation with a focus on how epistemic markers affect LLM-based judgments. The extraction was generally good but needed clarification between generation models (GPT-4, Newbing) and judge models (GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4-turbo, GPT-4o, Llama-3 models). The paper uses both automated metrics (Accuracy, VSR) and human evaluation with clear criteria.
